items.title: What does raising fidelity actually buy — and cost?
items.description: The checkout team from this unit's scenario had 4 fidelity levels to choose from. Drag the slider across them to see two genuinely different things move at once: how many hours it takes to build a prototype at that level, and how much you can trust its result to predict real behavior. Notice they don't move at the same rate.
items.compute: const level = Math.round(params.fidelityLevel); const hoursTable = [3, 10, 28, 90]; const signalTable = [30, 55, 75, 95]; const buildHours = hoursTable[level - 1]; const signalQuality = signalTable[level - 1]; return { buildHours, signalQuality };

items.title: How many chances to catch a mistake fit in your timeline?
items.description: The checkout team had about 4 weeks before their launch decision. A loop's length — how long one build-test-learn cycle takes — decides how many chances you get to catch a wrong idea inside that window. Drag the loop length to see how many full loops actually fit in a fixed 28-day timeline.
items.compute: const timelineDays = 28; const loopsPossible = Math.max(1, Math.floor(timelineDays / params.loopDays)); return { loopsPossible };
